'''Igor V. Minin''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Игорь Владиленович Минин}}) (born 22 March 1960 in [[Akademgorodok]], [[Novosibirsk]]), is a Russian [[physicist]], corresponding member of the Russian Academy of Metrology, and a full professor of Physics at [[Tomsk Polytechnic University]]. He became known for his contributions to new directions in optical physics: [[Terahertz tomography|terahertz 3D imaging]], Mesotronics ([[Mesoscopic physics|mesoscale]] [[photonics]]), and [[Structured light|subwavelength structured light]], including [[acoustics]] and surface [[plasmon]], as well as in high energy density physics.

==Biography==
Minin received his M.S. from [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 1982 and earned his Ph.D. Physics and Mathematics, specializing in radiophysics and quantum physics, from [[Saint Petersburg Electrotechnical University|St. Petersburg Electrotechnical Institute]] in 1986.<ref name="Karabchevsky">Alina Karabchevsky, [https://ab74d9ba-18a8-4d17-a106-49945088baf9.filesusr.com/ugd/12ada6_d4291fe0230149849d05f8855e3875bc.pdf ''Development of mesoscale photonics and plasmonics: a tribute to the jubilee of Professors Igor V. Minin and Oleg V. Minin''], SPIE Photonics Europe, 2020.</ref>

From 1981 to 1982 Minin worked part-time as a laboratory assistant at the Institute of Applied Physics in [[Akademgorodok]] that had been founded by his father, [[Vladilen F. Minin]], in 1966.

In March 2004, he defended his thesis for the advanced degree of Doctor of Technical Sciences, equivalent to a [[Habilitation#Equivalent degrees|Habilitation degree]].

Minin published several research monographs, including "Diffractional Optics of Millimetre Waves",<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.routledge.com/Diffractional-Optics-of-Millimetre-Waves/Minin-Minin/p/book/9780367454326 | title=Diffractional Optics of Millimetre Waves }}</ref> "Basic Principles of Fresnel Antenna Arrays"<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783540795582 | title=Basic Principles of Fresnel Antenna Arrays }}</ref> and later "Diffractive Optics and Nanophotonics: Resolution Below the Diffraction Limit"<ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite book|doi = 10.1007/978-3-319-24253-8|title = Diffractive Optics and Nanophotonics|series = SpringerBriefs in Physics|year = 2016|isbn = 978-3-319-24251-4 | last1=Minin | first1=Igor | last2=Minin | first2=Oleg | bibcode=2016don..book.....M }}</ref> and "The photonic hook: from Optics to Acoustics and Plasmonics".<ref>{{cite book | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-66945-4 | doi=10.1007/978-3-030-66945-4 | title=The Photonic Hook | series=SpringerBriefs in Physics | year=2021 | isbn=978-3-030-66944-7 | last1=Minin | first1=Oleg V. | last2=Minin | first2=Igor V. | bibcode=2021phho.book.....M | s2cid=234285298 }}</ref> Most of Minin's research was carried out with his twin brother [[Oleg V. Minin]].

In April 2007, the [[Federal Security Service|FSB of Russia]] accused the  [[List of twins#Scientists|Minin twins]] of revealing state secrets and sensitive information about research projects for the [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)]], following the publication of a book dedicated to the 40th anniversary of the Novosibirsk Institute of Applied Physics.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/27/world/europe/27iht-moscow.1.7268656.html ''Russia arrests 10 suspects in  murder of reporter''], "New York Times", August 27, 2007.</ref><ref>Alexandra Taranova, [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2010/09/21/2-scientists-held-in-murky-spy-case-a1622 ''2 Scientists Held in Murky Spy Case''], "Moscow Times", September 21, 2010; Natalya Krainova, [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2012/11/13/physicist-convicted-of-espionage-gets-parole-a19345 ''Physicist Convicted of Espionage Gets Parole''], "Moscow Times", November 13, 2012.</ref> This case was widely publicized, well-known scientists and [[Human rights defender|human rights activists]] spoke out in defense of the physics brothers. FSB investigators dropped their case against brothers, and prosecutors in [[Novosibirsk]] issued a rare apology to the scientists in July 2007.{{Citation needed|date=November 2020}}

Since [[Perestroika]] Minin had been a [[Professors in the United States#Visiting professor|visiting professor]] at multiple institutes internationally, including: [[Daimler AG#1998–2007: DaimlerChrysler|DaimlerChrysler AG]], [[DASA|Doiche Aerospace]], [[Technical University of Munich|Technische Universitat Munchen]] (Germany), [[Harbin Institute of Technology]], MMW [[State Key Laboratories|State Key Lab]], Nanjing, [[Beijing Institute of Technology]], [[Capital Normal University]] (China), [[Samsung Electronics]] (Korea), [[National University of Singapore]], [[Federico Santa María Technical University|Universidad Technica Federico Santa Maria]] (Chile) and [[University of Helsinki]] (Finland).

==Research==
Minin is a pioneer in the field of photonic jets generated by an arbitrary 3D shape particles.<ref name="Karabchevsky"/> In collaboration with his brother (twin) [[Oleg V. Minin]] 2015 he discovered the so-called photonic hook effect<ref name="ReferenceA"/><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|doi = 10.1007/978-3-030-66945-4|title = The photonic hook: from Optics to Acoustics and Plasmonics= SpringerBriefs in Physics| series=SpringerBriefs in Physics |year = 2021|isbn = 978-3-030-66945-4 | last1=Minin | first1=Oleg V. | last2=Minin | first2=Igor V. | s2cid=234285298 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1= Dholakia | first1=K. | last2= Bruce | first2=G.D. | title= Optical hooks | journal=   Nature Photonics| volume=13 | date=2019 | issue=4 | doi=10.1038/s41566-019-0403-9| pages=229–230| bibcode=2019NaPho..13..229D | s2cid=256704583 }}</ref> - artificially curved light beams with subwavelength curvature and beamwidth. Minin also experimentally demonstrated the existence of [[Acoustics]] and  [[surface plasmon]] photonic jet and photonic hook phenomena.<ref name=":0"/>

In dielectric structures with a Mie size parameter of order ten, which are in the region between the wave and geometric optics, he and his colleagues have discovered some new unusual effects, including super-resonance<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V. | title= The Superresonance: The Discovery That Was Not Done More Than One Hundred Years Ago | journal= [[Atmospheric and Oceanic Optics]] | volume=37 (3)| date=2024 | issue= | doi=10.1134/S1024856024700544| pages=293–301}}</ref> - the excitation of giant magnetic fields in dielectric mesoscale particles compared with the magnetic field in [[Neutron star]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1= Wang | first1=Z. | last2=Luk'yanchuk| first2=B. | last3=Yue | first3=L. | last4= Yan | first4=B. | last5=Yan | first5=B. | last6= Monks | first6=J. | last7= Dhama| first7=R. | last8=Minin | first8=O.V.| last9=Minin| first9=I.V.| last10=Huang| first10=S.| last11=Fedyanin| first11=A. | title=High order Fano resonances and giant magnetic fields in dielectric microspheres | journal= Scientific Reports| volume=9 | date=2019 | issue=1 | doi=10.1038/s41598-019-56783-3 | doi-access=free| page=20293| pmid=31889112 | pmc=6937277 | bibcode=2019NatSR...920293W }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| last3=Zhou | first3=S. | title=High-Order Fano Resonance in a Mesoscale Dielectric Sphere with a Low Refractive Index | journal= JETP Letters| volume=116 | date=2022 | issue=3 | doi=10.1134/S002136402260121X| pages=144–148| bibcode=2022JETPL.116..144M | s2cid=252820910 }}</ref> and based on high-order [[Fano resonance]].

With his brother, Minin founded the new field of "[[freezing]] droplet optics" with the discovery of unusual time domain effects of photonic hook<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=O.V. | last2=Minin | first2=I.V.|  last3=Cao | first3=Y. | title=Time Domain Self-bending Photonic Hook Beam Based on Freezing Water Droplet | journal= Scientific Reports | volume=13 | date=2023 | doi= 10.1038/s41598-023-34946-7 | page=7732 | doi-access=free | pmc=10182040 }}</ref> and Fano resonances.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.|  last3=Zhou | first3=S. | last4=Luk'yanchuk | first4=B.| title= High order Fano resonance in the time domain for a freezing water microdroplet | journal= Scientific Reports | volume=13 | date=2024 | doi= 10.1038/s41598-024-74425-1 | page=24118 | doi-access=free | pmc=11480091 }}</ref> He and his colleagues pioneered the study of the unusual optical properties of superresonance and photonic hooks in and near a rotating cylinder and sphere,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Tang | first1=H. | last2=Shi | first2=Z.|  last3=Li | first3=R. |  last4=We | first4=B. | last5=Gong | first5=S.| last6=Minin | first6=I.V. | last7=Minin | first7=O.V. |title=. Unusual Optical Phenomena Inside and Near a Rotating Sphere: the Photonic Hook and Resonance | journal=Optics Express| volume=32 | date=2024 | doi=10.1364/OE.518794| page=12950 | doi-access=free }}</ref> based on the optical analogue of [[Magnus effect]].

The presence of a number of interesting applications indicates a new promising direction in optics called "Mesotronics".<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| title=Mesotronics: Some New, Unusual Optical Effects | journal=Photonics | volume=9 | date=2022 | issue=10 | doi=10.3390/photonics9100762 | page=762 | bibcode=2022Photo...9..762M | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| last3= Luk'yanchuk| first3=B.| title=Mesophotonics: Physics and Systems at Mesoscale | chapter=Mesotronic era of dielectric photonics | editor-first1=Igor V. | editor-first2=Sylvain | editor-first3=Vasily N. | editor-last1=Minin | editor-last2=Lecler | editor-last3=Astratov | volume=121520D | date=2022 | doi= 10.1117/12.2634133| page=762| bibcode=2022SPIE12152E..0DM | isbn=978-1-5106-5180-7 | s2cid=248641915 }}</ref>

Minin has also made new investigations in the study of [[young stellar objects]], [[active galactic nucleus|active galactic nuclei]] and [[astrophysical jets]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Baranov | first1=P.F. | last2=Zatonov | first2=I.A.| title=Some pioneering research in laboratory simulation of scaled astrophysical phenomena by Russian physicists | journal= Journal of Physics: Conference Series| volume=1709 | date=2020 | issue=1 | doi=10.1088/1742-6596/1709/1/012003| article-number=012003| bibcode=2020JPhCS1709a2003B | s2cid=234566394 | doi-access=free }}</ref> by the analysis of pulse plasma jets produced by intense laser-matter interactions.

Minin is author or coauthor of over 450 research publications, including 22 monographs (12 in Russian, 9 in English and 1 in Chinese)<ref name="Karabchevsky"/> and more than 200 [[patent]]s. He is an editorial member of several international journals and chair of several international conferences.<ref>[https://spie.org/EPE/conferencedetails/photonics-and-plasmonics-at-the-mesoscale?SSO=1 The international society for optics and photonics].</ref>

==Awards==
* For his contribution to the theory of hypercumulation, Minin was awarded the medal of the Russian National Committee on Theoretical and Applied Mechanics of [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] named after Kh.A. Rakhmatulin in 2013.<ref>Medal Award List
named after Kh.A. Rakhmatulin [http://volnogaz.math.msu.su/pages/medal1.php]</ref>

* Russian medals named after V.I. Vernadsky and A. Nobel.<ref name="Karabchevsky"/>
